attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his post, stated as his own conclusion.

semantics.note: 'The media campaign worked, and Anthropic was able to close' says publicity helped get the round. Calling that causal is correct, and amount and date are kept.

contract.note: Counting any contribution, not sole cause, is a fair and ordinary reading. Asking for investor or decision evidence, not just the order of events, is reasonable. The 'estimate' accounting label doesn't affect the result.

evidence.note: Anthropic's own announcement confirms a $30B Series G on Feb 12, 2026. It credits customer demand and says nothing about a publicity effect. Company disclosure, so not an independent causal finding.
Lead investor GIC cites leadership, technical depth and enterprise adoption, and does not mention publicity. Its silence can't rule out a media effect.

reviews.rationale: The round's amount and date are confirmed. The causal part, that the Claude Code media campaign helped secure it, has no investor testimony or decision record in the packet. GIC's silence doesn't disprove it either. The causal claim is neither supported nor contradicted on this evidence.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his post.

semantics.note: Keeps both parts: startups burning cash, and Anthropic permitting $8+ of compute per subscription dollar until recently. 'Upwards of' is fairly rendered as eight dollars or more.

contract.note: 'Burn... in compute' next to 'annihilating cash' points to actual cost, but Zitron's linked source measures retail API value. The contract flags both readings. Under the API-value reading the ratio part would likely hold; under the actual-cost reading the packet has nothing on it.

evidence.note: Dated Jan 2026 analysis estimates roughly 8.1x (Pro) and 13.5x (Max) at retail API prices. That backs the API-value reading but measures neither actual compute cost nor any later cutoff.
Feb–Mar 2026 measurement finds large Max value at API prices, from a small sample. It is not a provider-cost record and doesn't show a later cutoff.

reviews.rationale: The packet shows permitted usage worth $8+ per dollar at API prices, but no actual compute-cost records. It doesn't show the 'until recently' change, and has no evidence on startups' cash burn. The result depends on reading compute as actual cost, and that part isn't settled.

attribution.note: Zitron's own description of the sequence of events 'as I see them'.

semantics.note: A general causal chain: lab price rises lead to startups cutting quality or raising prices, which leads to churn. The 'as labs raise prices' antecedent is kept and 'and/or' is preserved.

contract.note: Requiring all three causal links and real customer departures is an ordinary reading of 'leading to customer churn'. Counting extra token use as an effective price rise follows the speaker's own context.

evidence.note: Cursor ties its billing change to higher token use per request, one partial link. No measured supplier price rise and no churn data.
Lindy cut costs by moving to a cheaper model while watching retention. It doesn't show a supplier price rise or publish retention figures, so it neither confirms nor refutes the mechanism.

reviews.rationale: No matched evidence links a lab price rise to a startup's price or service change and then to measured customer departures. Cursor shows at most one link. Lindy is a different situation with no retention data. The packet doesn't settle the general mechanism.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his post.

semantics.note: Rendering 'represented' as 'resemble' is faithful, and 'have never' plus both named comparisons are kept. Framed as an observation, but it is a rejected analogy with no standard for similarity.

contract.note: The contract rightly declines to invent comparison metrics or similarity thresholds. Any score would rest on an interpretation the speaker didn't give.

reviews.rationale: Rejecting an analogy without naming companies, metrics, matched stages or how much similarity counts can't be tested. Scoring it would mean substituting new criteria for his claim. The packet has no evidence items, which is consistent with that.
